full_judgment:
9. Respondent Nos. 1-3 and 5 filed an affidavit- in-opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the Writ Petition. The case of the respondents, in short, is that the authority has not done anything without due process of law and in this respect the actions taken by the authority are not illegal; malafide and arbitrary. During the enquiry no violation of existing rules has occurred. Four women students submitted a written complaint against Mr Sanowar Hossain, Associate Professor of the Department of Drama and Dramatics and the University Authority formed a fact-finding committee on 5-5-2008. The committee took statements of all concerned with audio record and written statement. After proper analysis and scrutinising the allegations, the committee submitted a report to the Vice-Chancellor stating that the fact-finding committee found no proof of sexual harassment suggesting further enquiry. 

 12. Ms Sara Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the enquiry process carried on under section 44(3) of the Act is faulty as the minimum requirement of fairness was not followed. She further submits that four victims deposed before the enquiry committee stating sexual abuse and that their evidence was discarded on flimsy ground. She then submits that in a domestic enquiry the standard of proof of such an allegation must be 'on the balance of probability' and not 'beyond reasonable doubt'. She continues to submit that the Syndicate accepted the report in part and rejected another part without assigning any reason whatsoever. She then submits that this matter should be investigated afresh in the line of the guidelines formulated by this Court. She lastly submits that the University authority is considered in loco parentis in relation to the students but that the authority failed to discharge that obligation. 

 31. While finding that the allegations against Mr Sanowar Hossain were not true, the final enquiry committee stated that the allegations were not proved by any direct (প্রত্যক্ষ) witness beyond reasonable doubt. This finding of the committee is perverse as the victims stated in no uncertain terms that they were sexually harassed/abused by Mr Sanowar Hossain. What credit should be attached to the statements of the victims is a different matter, but it cannot be said that their evidence is not direct evidence. Section 134 of the Evidence Act requires no particular number of witnesses for proof of any fact. In the present case, as many as four victims and three witnesses deposed alleging sexual abused harassment and their evidence must be treated as direct and in our social condition, the evidence of the victims cannot be brushed aside in the manner it has been done. Ahmed, J of the Indian Supreme Court in the case of State of Maharashtra vs Chandraprakash Kewalchand Jain, AIR 1990 SC 658, while dealing with a rape case observed, "Courts must also realise that ordinarily a woman, more so a young girl, will not stake her reputation by levelling a false charge concerning her chastity (at p 665)". The same can be said in case of sexual harassment. 

 The victim-complainants were not provided with any copy of the evidence recorded or even of the report of any of the enquiries. The teacher had legal representation. The victim-complainants were denied opportunities to present witness in support of their complaints or to cross-examine witnesses presented by Mr Sanowar Hossain. Annexure-H is the proof that the victim-complainants were not supplied with the enquiry report, evidence in spite of filing application. 

 39. Ms Sara Hossain submits that the standard of proof to be applied in a disciplinary enquiry which is a domestic enquiry involving a person, who holds a position of trust, must be 'on the balance of probabilities' and not 'beyond reasonable doubt'. In support of her contention, she cites the case of President vs Shaukat AI, PLD 1971 SC 585. 

 41. From the case referred to above, it appears that the subject matter of these disciplinary proceedings is neither civil rights and duties or criminal liabilities. Therefore, the burden of proof in such cases, in essence, is the probability.
